pre_mortem: The strongest opposing case is that Dallas exploits Baltimore's seven allowed passing explosives and leads early. Henry then loses rushing opportunities while Williams gains them, creating a shared failure scenario. Even without that script flip, Henry's illustrative 18-carry result clears by less than three yards, while Baltimore has allowed six runs of 10-plus yards that could rescue Williams' total. Two-game samples do not resolve either player's workload distribution. These risks keep both selections at lean rather than strong.
slip_story: Both leans belong to a Baltimore-controls-the-ground-game story: Henry accumulates rushing work while Dallas moves away from Williams' rushing attempts. Prefer separate evaluation as singles; no 3–4-leg main slip is justified from these two edges, and no touchdown or depth-receiver leg is added merely to fill a ticket.
